name: session_status
description: Report whether the solve leaf has an active backend. Safe to call before `connect`. Returns the connected endpoint, backend kind, and the list of tools available in the current state.

outputSchema.description: Result of ``session.status``. It is safe to call before ``connect``.

leaf.description: Leaf name: solve | geometry | mesh | post

items.description: Static description of one tool/feature exposed by a leaf.

name: connect
description: Connect the solve leaf to a backend. Available backend kinds: ['pyfluent']. Pass `backend_kind` to choose, or omit it to auto-select. Backend-specific options (url/token/ip/port/...) go in `connect_kwargs` as a dict and are forwarded to the backend.

backend_kind.description: Backend kind to select from the configured backends.

items.description: Minimal connection descriptor surfaced to clients/UI for selection.

name: disconnect
description: Disconnect the solve leaf's active backend.

name: list_named_objects
description: Return a mapping of named-object collection paths to the names of the objects currently defined. Cached briefly to keep follow-up tool calls fast. Supports pagination: pass `limit` (>=1) and optional `offset` to slice the names of each collection; the response then includes a `_pagination` envelope with the original totals so the caller can request more if needed.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to include in the response.

offset.description: Number of items to skip before returning results.

name: find_named_object
description: Resolve a symbolic name (e.g. 'inlet-1') across every named-object collection. Returns a list of {collection_path, name, exact} matches sorted with exact matches first. Use this BEFORE generating code so you know which collection (wall, velocity_inlet, fluid_zone, ...) the user actually meant; if multiple matches exist, ask a follow-up question.

name.description: Name of the object, module, or setting being processed.

name: select_named_objects
description: Expand a glob pattern over a single named-object collection and return the matching names. Use this instead of hand-curating a long list when the user asks for 'all walls', 'all inlets', 'every fluid zone', etc. — it makes the selection reproducible and survives mesh re-numbering. Arguments: `collection` is the dotted path of the named-object family (e.g. 'setup.boundary_conditions.wall'); `pattern` is a Unix-shell-style glob (default `*`); `include_shadows` defaults to `true` for thermal wall families and is silently ignored for non-wall collections; `exclude` is an optional list of glob patterns to subtract from the result.

collection.description: Named-object collection or API collection to search.

pattern.description: Glob pattern used to select matching names.

include_shadows.description: Whether shadow objects should be included when applicable.

exclude.description: Optional glob patterns to remove from the selection.

name: find_api
description: Retrieve candidate Fluent settings APIs for a query from the bundled Fluent API catalog. Returns ranked hits as {path, kind, score, ...}. Use this to locate the dotted settings path that implements a property (e.g. query 'temperature wall' returns wall.thermal.temperature variants). Optional filters: `kinds` (Parameter, Command, Object, Group) and `under` (path prefix to scope the search).

query.description: Search text or user request to evaluate.

top_k.description: Maximum number of results to return.

kinds.description: Optional result kinds used to narrow the operation.

under.description: Optional path prefix used to scope the operation.

compact.description: Whether to enable or apply compact.

name: get_state
description: Return the current state of the requested settings paths. If `paths` is omitted, returns the global Fluids state summary. FAST PATH: pass `key` together with a single collection path in `paths` (e.g. paths=['setup.boundary_conditions.wall'], key='outer-wall') to fetch JUST that one named-object slice without dumping every sibling — saves substantial prompt tokens on big cases.

paths.description: Fluent object paths supplied to the operation.

key.description: Key used to look up or store the associated value.

name: get_targeted_context
description: Fetch active-status, state, named-objects, child-names, and allowed values for a focused set of paths in a single call. Use this for fast disambiguation before generating code.

paths_to_check.description: Fluent object paths to validate or inspect.

named_object_types.description: Named-object families that should be considered during lookup.

instance_state_fetch.description: Whether named-object instance state should be fetched.

name: get_help
description: Return docstring + child names + allowed values for a specific Fluent settings path. Use this to confirm semantics of an ambiguous parameter (e.g. 'turbulent_intensity' vs 'intensity') before emitting code.

path.description: Filesystem path or API path to process.

name: solver_status
description: Return solver readiness summary: initialized, iterations, residuals, solver_mode (steady|transient). Use this before deciding whether to emit run_calculation.iterate(...).

name: run_code
description: Execute Python code against the connected PyFluent solver session. The code runs with `solver` (and `session` alias) pre-injected in scope — use `solver.settings.<path>` to read or mutate the model. Returns stdout, stderr, and any `__return__` value. Prefer `get_state` / `get_targeted_context` for read-only queries.

code.description: Python code or command text to execute or validate.

name: validate_code
description: Dry-run / validate the generated code without applying side effects. Returns parse / type / semantic feedback for callers.

code.description: Python code or command text to execute or validate.

name: screenshot
description: Capture a PNG screenshot of the current model view. Returns `{format: 'png', data: <base64>}`.

view.description: Graphics view or camera preset requested by the caller.

name: manage_fluent
description:
Manage the fluent component lifecycle in Fluids One. Actions:
  • activate — start or resume the fluent component.
  • deactivate — cleanly stop fluent and free resources.
  • update — apply pending configuration changes.
  • refresh — force reload state from the server.
Returns a status dict.

action.description: Action name requested by the caller.

name: summarize_setup
description: Return the full solver setup summary — models, materials, boundary conditions, solver settings, discretization schemes, and limits — in a single call. Equivalent to Fluent's Report > Summary. Use this FIRST when the user asks 'show me my setup' or 'what is configured?'. Read-only.

name: simulation_report
description:
Generate or export a rich simulation report from the connected solver session. Actions:
  • generate — create a named simulation report.
  • export_html — export an existing report as HTML.
  • export_pdf — export as PDF.
  • export_pptx — export as PowerPoint.
  • list — list previously generated reports.
Returns the output path or report list.

action.description: Action name requested by the caller.

report_name.description: Report definition name targeted by the operation.

name: mesh_quality
description: Return live mesh quality metrics (skewness, orthogonal quality, aspect-ratio histograms) for the connected Fluent solver. When ``include_check`` is true the response also embeds the output of Fluent's ``mesh.check()`` command. Use this tool whenever the user asks 'show mesh quality', 'skewness', 'orthogonal quality', 'aspect ratio', or 'check mesh' — never route those intents through ``query_reports``.

name: list_fields
description: Enumerate the scalar / vector fields available in the loaded Fluent case (pressure, temperature, velocity-magnitude, wall-shear, …). Optional ``scope`` filters to cell/node/face domains (default 'any'). Returns a flat list ready to use in a report-definition, contour, vector, or one-shot integral. Requires a live session.

name: compare_files
description: Open two Fluent case/mesh files in two SEPARATE ephemeral PyFluent sessions and summarize the differences between them. Both sessions are launched headless (no_gui) and the cases are read with lightweight_setup=True for speed; the live workspace session, if any, is NOT touched. Returns a structured diff of global model state and per-family named-object name lists. Use for questions like 'what changed between these two cases?', 'compare A.cas.h5 and B.cas.h5'. The response includes a pre-rendered markdown table in the 'summary' field grouped by hierarchy. Reply with that 'summary' string verbatim — its column headers ARE the actual file names and a '—' cell means 'not present in that file'. Do NOT re-label files as 'File A' / 'File B', do NOT add a 'Change' column back, and do NOT paraphrase the table into bullet lists.

name: probe_path
description: Batch pre-flight probe for one or more Fluent settings paths. Returns ``{path: {exists, is_active, is_user_creatable, kind}}`` in a single round-trip. Use BEFORE writing to a path to verify (a) the path is a real schema node, (b) it is ACTIVE in the current solver mode (paths gated by other model toggles return ``is_active=false``), and (c) you may ``.create()`` under a NamedObject collection (``is_user_creatable``). Inactive paths are silently ignored by Fluent or raise ``InactiveObjectError`` at apply — this tool catches both cases up front. Requires a live session.

name: get_active_status
description: Batch active-status probe for one or more Fluent settings paths. Returns ``{path: bool}``. Inactive paths cannot be written — Fluent either silently ignores the write or raises ``InactiveObjectError`` at apply. Use this tool to gate URF / discretization / model-sub-knob writes whose activity depends on a sibling model toggle (e.g. ``setup.models.viscous.k_omega_model`` is inactive unless ``viscous.model='k-omega'``, ``solution.controls.p_v_controls.explicit_*`` is inactive under SIMPLE / SIMPLEC / PISO). Requires a live session.

name: get_allowed_values
description: Batch allowed-values probe for one or more Fluent enum / menu-style settings paths. Returns ``{path: [allowed_values]}``; paths with no allowed-values constraint return an empty list. Use BEFORE writing to an enum field (``viscous.model``, ``wall.thermal.thermal_condition``, ``spatial_discretization.discretization_scheme['mom']``, ...) so the chosen value is guaranteed to be accepted by Fluent. Requires a live session.

name: describe_named_object_template
description: Describe the field shape of a fresh child under a NamedObject collection (boundary conditions, cell-zone conditions, report definitions, materials, surfaces, expressions, ...). Returns ``{child_class, fields, is_active, is_user_creatable, create_command}`` where ``fields`` carries per-field ``{type_hint, is_active, is_read_only, is_user_creatable, allowed_values, min, max, default, units}``. Use BEFORE proposing ``set_named`` / ``multi_edit`` to learn which fields are required, which are read-only (computed by Fluent), and which carry an allowed-values constraint. Requires a live session.

name: describe_path
description: Batch unified descriptor for one or more Fluent settings paths. Composes the ``probe_path`` + ``get_allowed_values`` (+ ``describe_named_object_template`` / ``get_command_arguments`` when the path is a NamedObject collection or a Command) probes into a single ``PathDescriptor`` per path — one round-trip on the wire, one shape on the wire, ready to feed the recipe / validator grounder without stitching four different envelopes together. Every field defaults to ``null`` (meaning 'unknown / unavailable'); an empty ``allowed_values`` list carries 'the backend explicitly reports no allowed values', which is different from ``null`` (probe skipped or failed). Requires a live session.

name: export_surface_data
description:
Write geometry-linked scalar data to indexed, hashed NPZ and JSON files.

The response stays small. Local arrays retain exact connectivity and
invalid values; invalid data are counted rather than replaced with zero.
Node sampling aligns with vertices. Face sampling follows boundary-face
ordering; Fluent can supply adjacent-cell values when a boundary value is
unavailable, so values need not equal evaluation at the geometric centroid.
max_faces limits the exported selection after retrieval, not RPC memory.

name: read_live_monitor_history
description:
Read one bounded tail snapshot without starting/stopping shared streams.

Optional output_prefix exports this exact snapshot as JSON, CSV and PNG
with hashes. The MCP bridge also returns the PNG as image content. Use
logarithmic=True for positive residual curves; zero/negative values cause
an explicit export error rather than being clipped. Tail statistics are
descriptive only; they do not establish convergence.

Requires public ``get_monitor_set_data(..., start_index=...)`` support.
One extra point detects truncation at the scan cap. Above that cap the
exact total is unavailable: ``total_points`` is null and its lower bound
is explicit. Totals refer only to this client's current monitor buffer.
Coordinates remain the unmodified numeric monitor coordinates. Native
xlabel metadata is preserved separately as native_display_label, never
treated as proof of time/iteration meaning or units. Tail slopes are per
native numeric coordinate only; establish physical meaning independently.
All fetched values, including those outside the returned tail, must be
aligned and finite. An oversized series set is rejected, not filtered.
PyFluent allocates arrays for every series before this helper can cap them.

name: solver_progress
description:
Separate native iteration/time evidence from configured run controls.

Iteration is Fluent's expression value, not a zero-based count of work
completed by this tool. No stream, background poll, or solve is started.
The reference surface supplies a location for the read-only reduction.

name: route_report_files
description:
Route selected existing Report Files into a fresh local directory.

Preserve activation, definition mapping, and sampling frequency. An empty
new directory prevents an inherited filename from appending to prior work.
Redirect future writes; existing histories stay at their original paths.
Return requested/effective paths and verified rollback evidence on failure.

name: export_contour
description:
Create a native PNG with fixed scale and settings/camera provenance.

Explicitly load the supplied saved pair before plotting. This replaces
unsaved live state: preserve it before calling. A temporary contour/view is
deleted after export. Output files are never overwritten. The displayed
window changes, as it does for upstream screenshot workflows.

name: read_report_file_history
description:
Read a UTF-8/ASCII native Fluent Report File on the local MCP host.

Accepts a title string, then e.g. ("Iteration" "outlet-temp" "flow-time"),
then whitespace numeric rows (also Fortran D exponents). All columns are
retained as floats; the default coordinate is the first column. No integer
iteration assumption, sorting, filling, or interpolation is applied.

Reads at most max_bytes: the whole snapshot when it fits, otherwise a header
prefix (at most 64 KiB) and an aligned tail. Older rows/errors are NOT audited
in that case and the full point total is unknown. Errors in the inspected
window remain explicit even when outside the returned tail. At most 20
issue details are returned, with exact issue and rejection counts.

Every repeated/decreased coordinate starts a segment; this flags a possible
restart, not its cause. Segment indexes are zero-based and end-exclusive
within returned rows. A valid final row without newline is returned with
partial status because a live writer could still extend its last token.
No remote reads, path discovery, MCP registration, or access sandbox here:
the official MCP caller must enforce its own filesystem access policy.

name: join_history_segments
description:
Join bounded captured histories; retain conflicts and unavailable values.

Each segment requires source_id, sha256, axis{name,unit}, units, x and
aligned series arrays. Optional stage separates reset counters; optional
source_rows maps submitted samples to original source row indices. Hashes
are caller assertions. Establish common lineage, definitions, scaling,
units and equation activity first. Null means unavailable, never zero.
Equal coordinates collapse only exactly equal complete aligned vectors;
distinct variants remain with explicit errors. No interpolation/rebasing.

Gap detection is disabled unless expected_step is a positive number. With
it enabled, a gap is an adjacent unique-coordinate span strictly greater
than expected_step + step_tolerance in one stage. step_tolerance is an
explicit nonnegative absolute allowance in axis units, used ONLY for gap
checks. The default is exact; supply an allowance for rounded time axes.
Arithmetic uses exact ratios of the supplied numbers to avoid overflow or
rounding during the check. No missing coordinates are generated or counted,
and no regular grid or expected start/end is inferred.

coverage describes only the observed range of each stage. Per-column
nonnull/null counts refer to retained output rows, including conflicting
variants. duplicate_overlaps identifies collapsed rows; provenance.rows
contains all their source references. errors contains the output indices
and differing columns for each conflicting stage/x. status is 'conflict'
when errors exist, otherwise 'joined'; neither implies complete coverage
or live Fluent acceptance. Empty stages have null bounds.

source_id.description: Opaque source label; establish common lineage/scaling before joining

sha256.description: Caller assertion of source hash; helper does not verify file bytes

axis.description: Identical metadata across sources; requires name and unit

units.description: Full identical output-column map, including unavailable equations

stage.description: Separate coordinate domain for counter resets

source_rows.description: Optional original source-row indices for each submitted sample

name: inspect_mesh_file
description:
Return topology, raw-coordinate extents and boundary geometry with provenance.

``path`` and ``allowed_root`` must be absolute local paths on the MCP host.
The resolved regular file must stay below the resolved caller-owned root.
The caller must choose an authorized root; this function cannot establish
authorization. Symlink escapes, UNC/device/URI paths and data streams fail.

Only the evidenced Fluent 25.2 version-2 layouts in ``.cas.h5`` and
``.msh.h5`` are accepted. Every node and zone ID range must form an exact,
disjoint partition starting at 1. Boundary geometry uses intersections of
face-zone ranges and connectivity-block ranges, regardless of block names.
All boundary faces are inspected or the call fails; there is no sampling,
partial-success truncation, or automatic increase of resource limits.

``max_file_bytes`` bounds each of two full SHA-256 passes.
``max_read_bytes`` independently bounds the sum of declared decoded extents
of accessed datasets, and cumulative selected dataset/attribute bytes read.
Coordinate arrays, integer offsets and HDF5 caches add memory overhead.
Counts, total zones, blocks per group, connectivity extent and vertices per face have
separate limits. Interior-only blocks are checked structurally but their
payloads are not read; mixed blocks require all vertex counts for offsets.

Units are metadata, not an implicit conversion. Area and centroid methods,
normal winding limitations and uninspected interior semantics are returned
in ``limitations``. Unknown cell/node type labels remain null. Names never
determine a zone's type or flow role. No native volume semantics are used.

Requires h5py and numpy only. Raises ValueError for unsupported/invalid data
or limits, PermissionError for a root escape, RuntimeError for detected
source changes, and native I/O/HDF5 errors for unreadable/corrupt files.

name: compare_surface_datasets
description:
Compare scalar values after exact geometry matching, with no solver.

Select two absolute local .npz files. Each .json is inferred from that
selected filename in the same directory; JSON paths are never followed.
Verify NPZ bytes/SHA256, require identical explicit surface names, field,
complete field_metadata (including mapped SI units/domain), sampling and
boundary-value policy, then audit decoded boundary geometry in both modes.

Faces match by sorted exact 3D vertex-coordinate sets, with multiplicity.
Nodes match by exact coordinate groups, with multiplicity. Every duplicate
group within either input must have identical values (all NaNs count as
one invalid class); differing duplicate values refuse comparison even when
their multisets happen to agree. No pairing by row number is used.

absolute_tolerance must be finite/nonnegative. Only abs(B-A) > tolerance
counts as a changed finite pair; it never changes geometry or statistics.
Delta statistics use finite pairs only, give every sample equal weight,
and are None when no finite pair exists. Nonfinite coverage remains explicit.

Limits apply separately to each input. max_file_bytes (hard cap 512 MiB)
bounds compressed NPZ size; JSON has a fixed 1 MiB cap. max_array_bytes
(hard cap 1 GiB) bounds the SUM of decoded NPY members, including headers.
There are at most 128 arrays with 10000-byte headers. max_samples (hard cap
1000000) bounds each of total samples, total vertices and total faces.
Decoded extents/dtypes/shapes are checked before any array payload is read.

Raises ValueError for unsupported, ambiguous, incompatible, corrupt,
changing or excessive inputs. Filesystem errors may propagate. Successful
comparison proves only this recorded boundary-sampling contract; see the
returned limitations. This function writes no output and changes no files.

name: bundle_artifacts
description:
Create a new bounded ZIP with ``manifest.json`` and explicit artifact bytes.

``root`` must be an absolute local directory. Input/output paths may be
absolute or relative to it; resolved paths must remain inside it. The
output parent must already exist. No traversal, UNC/device paths, directory
crawling, remote fetching, implicit sidecars or overwrites are permitted.
Select 1..32 regular PNG/JSON/CSV/OUT/VW/NPZ/HTML files explicitly. Numbered
members (``artifacts/001.png`` etc.) map to root-relative source paths in
the manifest; identical basenames cannot collide. Duplicate source paths
or file identities are rejected. Source bytes are copied without changes.

Both byte limits are positive integers capped at 16 MiB. max_total_bytes
bounds the summed initial source extents; growing files are not chased.
max_expanded_bytes separately bounds the sum of uncompressed NPY members
across all selected NPZ files. NPZ needs NumPy and supports at most 128
flat numeric/boolean NPY v1/v2 members per file, with pickle forbidden.
JSON must parse; text must be UTF-8 (optional BOM). Nonfinite JSON/NPZ
numbers and standalone nonfinite/overflowing CSV/OUT/VW numbers fail.
PNG/HTML and arbitrary text syntax have the limitations in the manifest.

Each hash covers the exact bytes read from one identity-checked handle.
Before/after stat records, source-declared truncation/error flags and
incomplete text endings expose observed uncertainty. Source completion is
always unknown: packaging status ``ok`` proves neither finality nor shared
scientific lineage. Malformed JSON/NPZ cannot be validated and must be
retried after their writer finishes. A detected escape/replacement fails.

All selected content is checked before exclusively creating output. ZIP
source data is bounded as above; its manifest is capped at 256 KiB plus ZIP
overhead. The response contains ``zip`` (local path, relative path, bytes,
SHA-256), ``manifest`` and ``manifest_sha256``. MCP resource registration
and client retrieval belong to the caller. No Fluent dependency is loaded.
On failure, cleanup removes only the file exclusively created here when
its path still identifies our inode; cleanup failures annotate the error.
Validation and OS/decoder failures propagate; no partial success is hidden.

MCP returns a resource_uri and resource link for ZIP retrieval. The hash-checked registry holds at most 128 bundles, including pending calls, and lasts for this server process. Request cancellation does not stop an accepted publication: while the server runs, it retains ownership until failure cleanup or resource registration finishes. A cancelled successful publication still occupies a registry slot; its URI is artifact://mcp-additions/bundles/{zip_sha256}.

resource_uri.description: Fetch with MCP resources/read; expires with this server process; changed bytes are refused
